findings.summary: The export expands every lot/order into one row per conversion document without enforcing EXCEL_MAX_ROWS. Exact host evidence projects 1,807,231 rows, exceeding Excel's 1,048,576-row worksheet limit by 758,655, so the required ordinary single-sheet workbook cannot be produced within capacity and may fail, truncate data, or become invalid.

The nested flatMap/map pipeline materializes the entire expanded dataset in browser memory before worksheet generation. Output is unbounded by the declared maximum, and the unused EXCEL_MAX_ROWS constant provides no guard or controlled failure path, jeopardizing download availability at the evidenced annual scale.

unverified: No tests are shown for worksheet capacity boundaries, download behavior, truncation/reconciliation, or browser-memory failure handling.
The behavior of writeSingleBrowserWorksheet when passed more than 1,048,576 rows cannot be verified from the supplied diff.

findings.summary: displayedClosing omits supported fx_other consumptions, so the displayed closing balance is overstated by the fx_other total (observed as 1,494,440 TRY) and cannot reconcile exactly.
The change returns only a computed closing value; it does not display the required exact opening, inflow, per-consumer-category outflow, conversion, and closing turnover.

unverified: No tests are shown proving exact reconciliation for expense, fx_eur, and fx_other, including mixed-consumption pools, empty categories, and numeric precision behavior.
The supplied diff does not show the definitions or behavior of Pool and sum, so type safety, unit consistency, rounding, overflow, and invalid-input handling cannot be verified.

findings.summary: Each detail amount is rounded independently, so the returned amounts are not guaranteed to sum to the currency-rounded source amount. This directly violates exact-to-the-cent reconciliation and matches the reported aggregate drift; allocate rounded minor units and distribute the residual deterministically.

The function does not validate or normalize shares, so shares whose sum differs from 1 cannot preserve the source total even before rounding; non-finite values and an empty array are also accepted without a defined failure mode.

Binary floating-point multiplication and Math.round have unsafe behavior near half-cent boundaries and for large or non-finite values, which can produce incorrect currency rounding; integer minor-unit or decimal arithmetic with explicit rounding semantics is needed.

unverified: No tests are shown for residual-cent distribution, positive and negative amounts, zero amounts, fractional shares, half-cent boundaries, malformed shares, or large values.
The required currency rounding rule, treatment of negative values, and deterministic tie-breaking policy for residual allocation are unspecified.

findings.summary: The verify script no longer runs `prisma generate`, so generated clients are not refreshed before typecheck after schema changes.
The `|| echo existing Prisma mismatch` fallback converts every `tsc --noEmit` failure into a successful script exit, allowing genuine type errors to pass the release gate.
A temporary reviewer probe is added to the release tree despite the frozen acceptance criterion explicitly excluding reviewer probes.
Private review-run scratch notes are added to the release tree despite the frozen acceptance criterion excluding private root-cause scratch material.
